active_themes.label: Blockade Turns Kinetic
active_themes.summary: Day 118 of this standoff, and today marks an escalation in kind, not just tone: a reported U.S. missile strike on a ship evading the blockade, plus a new Trump demand for compensation from Iran, both close off room for a quick Hormuz deal. Oil is pushing back toward $90 as a result. What remains open: whether Iran responds directly to the strike, which would be the signal this has moved from enforcement to open conflict.

active_themes.label: Rotation Confirmed, Not Noise
active_themes.summary: The Nasdaq underperformed the Dow for a second straight session today (down 0.6% versus the Dow's 0.34%), following yesterday's 0.32% versus 0.11% gap — that's now a repeating pattern, not a one-day fluke. Oil-driven risk-off is hitting growth stocks harder than defensive industrials on back-to-back days, which is the mechanism to keep watching.

active_themes.label: Gold Wins the Tug-of-War
active_themes.summary: Gold reversed back up to a two-month high today, meaning the safe-haven demand from escalating Iran tension outweighed the rate-cut-clouding drag from rising oil that pushed gold down yesterday — a reminder that gold can swing on whichever fear is loudest that day. The larger credibility question — what a future Fed cut means if it looks political rather than earned — remains unresolved and now has one more hawkish data point working against it (see Fed driver below).

active_themes.label: A Fed Voice Pushes Back
active_themes.summary: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, who dissented at last month's meeting, said today that current rates aren't meaningfully restrictive and multiple hikes — not cuts — may be needed, a direct counterweight to the case the administration is building off last week's weak jobs report. No new development today on the legal fight over Governor Cook's removal itself; what remains open is whether other officials side with Hammack's hawkish read or with the jobs-data dovish case, which will show whether the committee is unified or fracturing under pressure.

open_watchlist.condition: Whether a court challenge or ruling directly addresses Trump's renewed attempt to remove Governor Cook.
open_watchlist.meaning: A ruling reaffirming Fed independence keeps this a pressure campaign; an actual removal would be the first real breach of Fed independence in modern history.

open_watchlist.condition: Whether the next jobless claims or payroll revisions confirm or reverse today's job-loss print.
open_watchlist.meaning: Confirmation would mean the labor market is genuinely cracking, not just one noisy month, strengthening the case for a real Fed cut.

open_watchlist.condition: Whether the Nasdaq's rate-cut-driven rally extends or fades as more officials comment on the Cook situation.
open_watchlist.meaning: A fading rally would signal markets are starting to worry more about Fed credibility than they are excited about cheaper money.

open_watchlist.condition: Oil (Brent) gives back this week's 2% gain and Hormuz talks show a concrete reopening signal, rather than continuing to climb on stalled negotiations.
open_watchlist.meaning: Would confirm today's reversal was a one-day negotiating setback, not the start of a real breakdown.

open_watchlist.condition: The next inflation report shows core prices accelerating rather than cooling, arriving alongside oil's move higher.
open_watchlist.meaning: Would hand the Fed a genuine data-based reason to hold, deepening the credibility fight over any future cut rather than easing it.

open_watchlist.condition: The rupee's slide past today's two-week low continues or stabilizes as oil's price move plays out.
open_watchlist.meaning: A currency that keeps weakening on oil costs signals the Hormuz risk is spreading beyond energy markets into broader emerging-market stress.

open_watchlist.condition: Iran retaliates directly against a U.S. or allied vessel or asset following today's strike.
open_watchlist.meaning: Confirms this has moved from blockade enforcement to open conflict, and puts oil's move toward $95+ on the table.

open_watchlist.condition: The next CPI print shows core prices (inflation excluding food and energy) accelerating alongside oil's climb toward $90.
open_watchlist.meaning: Would confirm the stagflation setup — rising prices and slowing growth at once — that makes any Fed rate cut look premature.

open_watchlist.condition: The Nasdaq underperforms the Dow for a third straight session.
open_watchlist.meaning: Would turn the two-day rotation into an established trend rather than an Iran-headline reaction.

open_watchlist.condition: A second Fed regional president publicly backs Hammack's hawkish, no-cuts stance within the next week.
open_watchlist.meaning: Would signal a real split inside the Fed, not just one dissenting voice, deepening the credibility question around any future cut.
